recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Future edits to the remaining DeviceRequest/VisionPrescription open issue should be handled through that separate issue family rather than by reopening this Request actionability clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-11434 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core workflow change request raised against DSTU2. It argued that prescriptions and orders should remain distinct and was resolved by adding a Request usage note explaining that requests may be partially specified, not immediately actionable, and not necessarily ever sent for fulfillment.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn import commit 83f1205cc1f012816734622c56ee12d93a24212d (svn build@10162), which added the requested three-paragraph note under the Request Resource Pattern section of source/workflow.html. Later edits modernized resource names and spelling without changing the approved meaning.
additional_context: The current combined-branch source/workflow.html contains the approved note. The nearby remaining DeviceRequest/VisionPrescription Open Issues text is governed by a separate issue family: FHIR-39066 removed SupplyRequest from that workflow question, and existing combined-branch audits for FHIR-11217 and FHIR-40597 cover the VisionPrescription/DeviceRequest boundary decisions. Community searches found no directly relevant contrary Zulip or Confluence evidence for FHIR-11434.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The empty audit commit records that current active workflow source already satisfies FHIR-11434 by explaining that order-intent requests authorize something while actionability and fulfillment can depend on context and later information.
